minutes.headline: Sewer Commission raised the minimum connection charge and let ReBoot's overdue sewer bill ride on a $2,000 good-faith payment.
minutes.summary: After a public hearing, the commission voted to raise the minimum residential connection charge to match a Leominster increase. It then took up ReBoot restaurant's non-compliance with its sewer payment agreement, with a liquor-license review pending on May 21. It agreed to continue the matter to the end of the month rather than vote, in return for a $2,000 payment. A member announced he is resigning, and the business manager reported on Munis software problems and delinquent bills.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered.

votes.motion: Increase the minimum residential connection charge from $2,250 to $3,900 as written

budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager gave the third quarter commitment amount and asked for a vote.
The hearing was on raising the charge, a direct result of Leominster raising its connection fee in the new IMA. Commissioners said it was out of their control.
Commissioners were shocked at the cost of the proposals. Bill asked Wright-Pierce for a cheaper approach on manhole repair specs and pump replacement scope.
Receipts and expenditures to date were summarized. Third quarter money is still outstanding, and betterments and interest are forecast.
The agreement required weekly payments and full payment of future bills. A balance is outstanding and only a small amount has been paid since December.
ReBoot offered a $2,000 payment, and the May bill is also coming.

budget_items.topic: Green Communities grant for pumps and VFDs
budget_items.what_was_said: The estimated pump and VFD cost is stated without freight, and the maximum grant award is also stated. The grant depends on showing significant energy savings.
Delinquent balances were moved to tax bills. Missing demands on bills cost the commission revenue, and many third quarter bills are unpaid.

transfers.description: Delinquent prior-year sewer balances transferred to tax bills

decisions.decision: No vote on ReBoot. The matter is continued to the end of the month under the existing agreement, with a $2,000 good-faith payment expected April 10 and updates on the April 30 and May 14 agendas.
Wright-Pierce will be on the next meeting's agenda once they respond to Bill's requests.
The chair will pursue a short presentation to the select board on clogs from wipes. Staff will also post on the town website and Facebook pages and include a color bill insert with the May bills.
A member announced he is resigning, staying through May as needed.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to raise the minimum residential connection charge as written, after a public hearing.
The commission took no vote on ReBoot's non-compliance with its sewer payment agreement and continued the matter to the end of the month.
A an amount as heard good-faith payment from ReBoot was expected the next day, with updates set for the April 30 and May 14 agendas.
The commission accepted the third quarter commitment, and a member announced he is resigning, staying through May as needed.
Commissioners agreed to a public notice campaign on clogs from wipes, and Wright-Pierce's engineering proposals were held for the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The higher minimum connection charge is a one-time cost for new sewer connections, and the minutes tie it to a Leominster increase in the new intermunicipal agreement.
An unpaid commercial sewer balance and many unpaid third quarter bills affect the revenue the commission collects, and the minutes say missing demands on bills cost it revenue.
Engineering proposals that commissioners found costly, and a grant-dependent pump replacement, bear on future sewer rates and capital costs.
watch_next: April 30 and May 14 Sewer Commission agendas, where ReBoot updates are scheduled.
May 21 liquor-license review for ReBoot, which the commission's handling of the payment agreement bears on.
